title: A single checkout failure can later produce a sustained-outage alarm
description:
W8 follow-up F5. Source at aa1ad12: src/store/mod.rs:179-201.

One failed checkout followed by idle time reaches the 2000 ms sustained failure alarm without another failure sample. Distinguish elapsed time since one failure from demonstrated sustained checkout failure, and verify isolated-failure and persistent-failure cases without weakening outage alarms.

title: A duplicate external resource id can end the engine
description:
W8 follow-up F2. Source at aa1ad12: src/store/business.rs:486-496; src/engine.rs:852; src/bin/engine.rs:77-79.

When a provider returns an external id already attached to another create, the new external_id_attached refusal is fatal on engine settlement and automatic reconciliation paths. A provider identity anomaly can repeatedly end the process until its start limit. Park or report the affected operation without repeating the provider purchase. Verify the duplicate-id case preserves one attachment and no extra debit while the engine remains operable.

title: Iteration arguments can override the selected phase set
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tools/iteration.sh:25 appends arbitrary arguments after --phase iteration. A later --phase all or another selector replaces the intended W7/controls set, and --help exits without running it. Not higher: caller-controlled fixture invocation, with no runtime policy effect. Smallest fix: reject phase/help overrides or explicitly document and validate the permitted forwarded arguments. Verify: attempt a second phase selector and help, and ensure the command cannot report a completed iteration without its intended inventory.

title: Rejected credentials stay latched in memory until restart
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/engine/reconciliation.rs:136-139` latches a credential rejection in memory with no rotation or automatic health reset in this slice.

Why not higher: documented; unsent creates fail and release their money.

Smallest fix: re-read credential health from the store on rotation, or reset the latch on an operator action. Verify a rotated credential is used without a restart.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Housekeeping skip traces omit the underlying database code
description:
W8 follow-up F8. Source at aa1ad12: src/api/mod.rs:1540,1550,1560.

housekeeping_tick_skipped retains only two error contexts, which can omit the underlying PostgreSQL SQLSTATE. Preserve useful diagnostic cause data without exposing credentials or changing skip policy.

title: Deletion and resolution validate external ids differently
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 19 (a reader suggestion rated as a defect; round 2); PR #7 review-bot thread on `reconciliation.rs:616`; widened by the W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/engine/deletion.rs:36` accepts `.` in an external id; `src/engine/reconciliation.rs:611-616` does not. A dotted provider id can pass delete and be refused by resolution evidence filtering; the audit found that a dotted id also marks the whole account pass incomplete.

Why not higher: the simulator never generates a dotted id.

Smallest fix: align both with the pinned opaque-id grammar. Verify an exact dotted correlator through confirmation and deletion, and rejection of malformed evidence.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Control evidence filenames collide across parent evidence stems
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/controls.py:121-125 names red manifests only from their defect in evidence.parent, ignoring evidence.stem. Two runs writing distinct parent manifests into one directory overwrite the same child paths and invalidate the earlier parent references. Not higher: private evidence collision; child assertion results and separate-directory runs remain valid. Smallest fix: include the parent stem or use an invocation-owned child directory. Verify: write two distinct parent stems under one directory and check that both retain distinct, unchanged child manifests.

title: An early release-probe failure writes no parent controls manifest
description:
Severity P2. Source: W5 Run item 5 (a reader rated it P3 in round 2; the Run Manager rated it P2); carried as W6 Run item 5. Evidence at b037383: `tests/postgres/controls.py:60` returns 1 when the direct helper probe fails, before writing the phase evidence file. The phase still exits nonzero, but the parent manifest and its pointers are missing.

Why not higher: the failure is not masked; only its evidence is incomplete.

Smallest fix: write a failing parent manifest with the child pointer before returning. Verify with a deliberate helper failure.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A non-UTF-8 database URL can appear in startup diagnostics
description:
W8 follow-up F11. Source at aa1ad12: src/entry.rs:28-29; src/bin/api.rs:24; src/bin/engine.rs:53; src/bin/recovery.rs:117.

Preexisting: a non-UTF-8 PROVISIOND_DATABASE_URL produces a VarError whose displayed value can include the database password on stderr and in the supervisor journal. Report a fixed redacted configuration error instead. Verify with an isolated invalid-byte environment value containing a sentinel and assert the sentinel never appears in any diagnostic. This predates the W8 change and is tracked separately.

title: Enrolment disclosure says supported credential revocation is unavailable
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/api/mod.rs:474,492-493,314-332. The enrolment response says revocation is outside the prototype although the recovery route replaces the spending credential and advances its generation. Not higher: the misleading disclosure does not bypass authentication or generation enforcement. Smallest fix: describe the supported recovery replacement route and its limits. Verify: compare the enrolment disclosure with successful recovery-only replacement and rejection of the old token.

title: Malformed keys listing or any repeating per-row error ends the periodic pass and the engine
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 16 (two readers, one P3 raised to P2; round 1); widened by the W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `keys.as_array().context(...)` in `src/engine/reconciliation.rs:453` fails on a wrong-shape success, which ends the periodic component and the engine (`src/bin/engine.rs:64-75`). The audit found the same for any per-row error that repeats in the one-second pass.

Why not higher: only a wrong-shape provider success reaches it; it fails closed, with no invented absence and no money effect.

Smallest fix: handle malformed evidence and per-row errors locally (mark the pass incomplete) and keep the component running. Verify the pass continues after one malformed listing.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: W5 observer termination races the 20 ms sampler
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #6 review-bot thread (Minor); carried as W6 Run item 12. Evidence at b037383: `tests/postgres/w5_accounting.py:203` terminates the observer only while it is `idle`; a statement landing during a sample matches no row and the assertion fails before observer loss. Correct runs can fail.

Why not higher: fails closed; it cannot make a broken run green.

Smallest fix: poll, with a bound, until this observer is idle, then terminate only its PID. Verify by repeated runs of the case.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).
notes: W8 acceptance update: priority P1 for the observed fail-closed setup race. Commit bc435f3 adds a bounded same-PID idle wait only to failure_run, including saturation; the reconnect call site still performs a one-shot idle termination. Keep this issue open under the two-round tooling limit. A missed planned outage is not a pass. Final run and partial-fix scope: evidence/w8/report.md. The earlier P2 assessment is superseded for W8 acceptance; no claim that all callers are fixed.

title: Measure the housekeeping timeout lower bound from its own checkout start
description: PR11 follow-up F33. Source at e0ec53f: tests/postgres/w4_round2.py:209-220. The housekeeping checkout can start before the held-read gate wait returns, but elapsed time starts afterward; a valid 250 ms timeout can therefore measure less than .25 and fail the fixture. P2 false rejection, not a false pass; typed timeout, pending held request and same-process recovery are separately asserted. Remove the unrelated lower bound or derive it from an actual housekeeping checkout start, preserving all fault/context/upper-bound assertions. Verify the captured earlier-start schedule is accepted and missing faults remain rejected.

title: Share the exact SQLSTATE diagnostic formatter
description: W8 final Standards follow-up F30. Source at 35ecf701: src/store/migration.rs:181 and src/store/mod.rs:326. Both format the same PostgreSQL code/message pair as SQLSTATE code: message. Current output agrees; P3 duplication with no observed behavioral defect. Extract only the common formatting while preserving each connection-stage context, exact server reason and SQLSTATE. Verify both migration and ordinary connection diagnostics against the existing failure fixtures.

title: W7 causal summaries retain stale names and constant values
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: tests/postgres/w7.py:196-197,220,242-243,697-705; tests/postgres/harness.py:326-328,368-369. The summary calls a step-3 snapshot step2 and reports latest_generation=4 after asserting 6; other causal fields are constants. Not higher: measured assertions remain available and no runtime defect is demonstrated. Smallest fix: derive summaries from asserted observations or explicitly identify expected values, including consistent scenario evidence descriptions. Verify: compare summaries with the corresponding recorded state.

title: New deficiency CHECK constraints have generated names
description:
Severity P3. Source: W6 Run item 24 (round 4). Evidence at b037383: the cause/clamped_sats and absorbed-time checks in `migrations/0003-reconciliation.sql:95-97,132` have generated names, which later migrations may need to reference.

Fix: give them explicit names in a later schema migration, verified against `pg_constraint`.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A clean pre-admission driver closure is rejected by the fixture startup retry shape
description: W8 follow-up F27. Observed at b1b0c721: tests/postgres/workflow.py:198-218, W5 settlement_reply successor. The canonical run recorded only client keepalive/admission-check events followed by driver_closed and supervisor_drained, with no session_admitted, generation or business work and no armed transport fault. The failed 250 ms checkout invocation was retained, but the pre-admission allowlist accepts driver_closed_unused and rejects driver_closed, so the fixture refused its otherwise bounded deployment repeat. This is a fail-closed test failure, not a product success or a false pass. Extend the predicate only with evidence of an unused pre-admission session and preserve rejection after admission, armed faults and defect builds. Verify the captured trace is eligible while admitted or business-work traces remain refused. The failed canonical must remain recorded even if a later focused run passes.
notes: Clarification for the recorded canonical W5 failure at b1b0c721: the missing driver_closed entry in tests/postgres/workflow.py:201-214 explains why the fixture rejected that run's pre-admission event trace. This identifies the immediate test-rejection cause only. The cause of the standby's delay in that run and the outcome of a corrected retry are both unmeasured.

title: The publication transformation omits added manifest metadata
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: evidence/w7/publication-transform.json:8 says full manifests changed only for paths and raw stream fields, yet canonical.json:20,222 and canonical-w7.json:5989-5991 contain added published_as metadata, including inside embedded manifests. report.md:36-37 names the field, but the transformation record does not account for its additions. Not higher: additive provenance metadata, with no demonstrated scenario-result change. Smallest fix: disclose these insertions in the transformation record and distinguish original manifest fields. Verify: compare original/published object keys and reconcile every added field with the declared transform.

title: Allow a bounded fixture wait to follow a widened visibility window
description: Severity P2. The W8 lossy recovery fixture computes its wait once from the first complete account-pass snapshot (tests/postgres/w7.py:436), while later polls validate the current effective window. A later create observation can widen that window after the first pass, so a correct runtime may be rejected at the earlier fixture deadline. The absolute 180-second limit is finite and current assertions remain strict; this fails closed, never accepts early absence. This timing order was not observed in the retained controlled runs. Smallest follow-up: recompute eligibility from each read while retaining one absolute bounded deadline, and demonstrate a sample arriving after the first snapshot.

title: Tracker ignore list misses schema-migration vacuum copies
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #8 review-bot thread (Minor) on `.beads/.gitignore:12`. Evidence at 6568cba: `.beads/.gitignore:7-9` says the `.<db>.schema-migration-<run>.vacuum-*` copies that a failed `br doctor migrate-schema` can leave are ignored, but the only matching pattern is `*.vacuum-wal-cert*`. `git check-ignore --no-index` exits 1 for `.beads/.beads.db.schema-migration-1.vacuum`, `.vacuum-wal` and `.vacuum-shm`, and 0 only for `.vacuum-wal-cert`, so `git add .beads/` can stage a database copy.

Why not higher: tracker metadata only; it needs a failed schema migration and an unchecked `git add`, and the staged diff shows the files before a commit.

Smallest fix: add `*.vacuum`, `*.vacuum-wal` and `*.vacuum-shm` to `.beads/.gitignore`. Verify `git check-ignore --no-index` exits 0 for all four names.

Raised on PR #8 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/8#discussion_r4565231710).

title: The W7 rollback scenario never activates unbound settlement replay
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/api/funding.rs:191-196; tests/postgres/w7.py:293-313,330-342. The scenario loses allocated deposits but posts settlements only to a retained destination, so it never activates the missing-binding branch. Not higher: the existing branch skips unbound evidence correctly and no financial counterexample is shown. Smallest fix: post a settled observation for an allocation removed by the actual restore. Verify: observe the unbound trace, no invented deposit or credit, valid retained replay, and completed phase 3.

title: A supplied reporting file can identify itself as absent
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/recovery.rs:43-51; src/bin/recovery.rs:95-102. A supplied JSON object containing only reporting_input=absent is indistinguishable from the internal missing-input marker and is retained as absent. Not higher: loss endpoints remain unknown and no finite certificate is accepted. Smallest fix: track input availability outside user-controlled evidence content. Verify: compare omitted input with an explicitly supplied absent marker and preserve unknown loss bounds.

title: The pre-lock child sets its own components-stopped diagnostic
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/entry.rs:94-99; src/bin/recovery.rs:67-70. The engine sets PROVISIOND_COMPONENTS_STOPPED=yes for its child, which then checks that same flag; the flag is not independent stop or fence evidence. Not higher: this runs before startup lock or generation and does not itself authorize unsafe database authority. Smallest fix: clarify diagnostic ownership and meaning while retaining the prescribed phases. Verify: compare the wording with actual deployment stop and fence evidence.

title: Retained-history capacity: no receipt resource index, and housekeeping shares the single read checkout
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #5 known limits; W4 audit item 9. Evidence at b037383: receipts are permanent and `idempotency_records` (`migrations/0001-core.sql:123-129`) has no `resource_id` index; `SETTLED_RETENTION` (`src/api/mod.rs:40`) and `operation_history` (`src/api/mod.rs:31-35`) aggregate receipts by `resource_id`. The API store has one read session with a 250 ms checkout bound (`src/entry.rs:46`) shared by customers and housekeeping. Measured at 20,000 settled operations and 1,000,000 receipts with three concurrent readers: housekeeping missed its checkout and the API exited 1. Each operations-list page also aggregates the whole history before its limit.

Why not higher: fails closed (exit, no wrong data); the measured scale is beyond the local profile.

Smallest fix: add a `resource_id` index (or a receipt-to-operation index) and bound the list aggregation by the page. Verify by rerunning the retention scale matrix at that size with three readers. Related: retired-history reads item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A transient accept() error stops the API
description:
Severity P2 (rating confirmed by the follow-up ledger review). Source: W5 audit item 4; carried as W6 Run item 8. Evidence at b037383: any `listener.accept()` error on the customer or operator listener (`src/api/mod.rs:1245`, `:1253`) ends `serve()` and the API exits 1 until an operator restarts it. Handlers go into an unbounded `JoinSet`, and no credential is needed to open connections, so descriptor exhaustion (`EMFILE`) from idle loopback connections is plausible.

Why not higher: both listeners are loopback-only (`docs/scope.md:146`), so the attacker is a local process; the profile's failure model is exit and supervisor or operator restart followed by keyed replay (`docs/scope.md:157-159`; OVR-18); no money or data loss. (Corrected 2026-11-13: the earlier basis cited `docs/scope.md`'s saturation row, which covers database connection exhaustion, not listener descriptors.)

Smallest fix: log, back off and keep accepting on transient errors. Verify with an attributed transient accept failure.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: The canonical W7 suite bypasses engine-supervised pre-lock preparation
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/entry.rs:70-110; tests/postgres/w7.py:79-85,204-206,380-383,564-565,764-765. Canonical recovery helpers manually prepare step 1 before engine startup, and no committed PostgreSQL scenario asserts pre_lock_actor_started. Not higher: no incorrect runtime ordering is demonstrated and manual preparation is exercised. Smallest fix: add a focused real-engine startup from step 0 using the existing child. Verify: observe the loss report and acknowledged step 1 before lock and generation acquisition, plus owned-child cleanup.

title: A failed reread erases earlier reconciliation identifiers
description:
Severity P1 (re-rated from P2 on 2026-11-13; older than W7, review-preexisting): a requirement made false. OPS-13 requires the surviving provider-side identifiers to be preserved in the error details, and OPS-27's duplicate row requires both candidates to be surfaced; replacing them with an empty set after a failed reread makes both false. The original "why not higher" below is superseded by this re-rate. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/engine/reconciliation.rs:603-604` replaces `provider_identifiers.reconciliation` with the latest search's set, which is empty after a failed or partial read, so ids found earlier (for example two candidates) disappear from the error details until a later complete search finds them again. The money flags (`in_progress`, `single_match`) are kept and nothing is attached.

Why not higher: no attachment or money effect; only operator-visible evidence is lost temporarily.

Smallest fix: keep the union of observed safe ids separately from the latest verdict. Verify with two candidates followed by a failed reread.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).
close_reason: Safe provider identifier union survives failed and partial rereads independently of latest authority and money flags. Historical unchanged runtime fails the intended assertion; final canonical W6 case passes. See evidence/w8/report.md and regressions.json. Live provider-fault-only arm was not reachable.

title: D-12 still lists only fenced methods
description:
Severity P3. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `attach_details` and `land_create` no longer check the generation fence themselves; they rely on the caller's guard (a fenced settlement, or the resolution's status guard in the operator receipt transaction). `docs/decisions.md` D-12 does not say so. Documentation only; every caller holds the guard.

Fix: amend D-12 to name the guard each caller holds.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Name alarm delay and reported threshold together
description: W8 final Standards follow-up F29. Source at 35ecf701: src/store/accounting.rs:250-251 and src/store/mod.rs:186-199. The same sustained-alarm duration is repeated as a timer/comparison duration and a numeric emitted threshold. There is no measured mismatch, so this is P3 maintenance only. Derive the reported milliseconds from a named duration at each alarm site. Do not unify the independently owned Store-retry default with the checkout-alarm threshold merely because both currently equal two seconds. Verify alarm timing/value pairs without changing D-6/D-70 policy.

title: Admin effective-tenant overrides require a UUID
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 18 (round 2); PR #7 review-bot thread on `operator.rs:196`. Evidence at b037383: `src/api/operator.rs:195` parses the effective-tenant override as a UUID. API-6 and DOM-1 allow 1-128 characters from letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:` and `-`, so a valid tenant id such as `agent-7` is refused before the scoped lookup.

Why not higher: ordinary enrolment generates UUIDs, so the supported path is unaffected.

Smallest fix: validate the pinned identifier grammar instead of UUID syntax. Verify non-UUID tenant scoping on live and retained targets, and privacy for malformed and unknown tenants.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A failed result read obscures an acknowledged recovery action
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/bin/recovery.rs:70-79,116-124; src/recovery.rs:209-212,239-243,276-280; src/entry.rs:104-108. Prepare, close and parent commit before a separate result read; read failure becomes generic exit 1, and supervised preparation aborts that startup. Not higher: acknowledged durable state survives and no repeated unsafe action is shown. Smallest fix: distinguish acknowledged action completion from failed result retrieval and direct the operator to inspect retained state. Verify: fail only the post-commit read for each action and inspect the retained result.

title: A non-array rail reply stops the API
description:
Severity P2 (rating confirmed by the follow-up ledger review). Source: W5 audit item 2; carried as W6 Run item 7. Evidence at b037383: a 200 `/settlements` reply with valid JSON that is not an array fails `as_array().context("rail observation array")` (`src/api/funding.rs:133`), ends the funding watcher and the API exits 1 (`task_stopped`, `src/api/mod.rs:1236`; `src/bin/api.rs`). Transport errors, non-200, unparseable and oversized replies are retried (`funding.rs:140`).

Why not higher: only the trusted loopback rail adapter can produce it; no false credit; documented bounded failure handling (`docs/scope.md`), and a W4 lifecycle test uses this fault as its exit trigger.

Smallest fix: treat it as an unavailable observation and retry. The W4 test (`tests/postgres/w4_round2.py:163-178`) needs a new trigger. Verify a later valid observation is credited.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Recovery shutdown failures can exit without an explanatory error
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/bin/recovery.rs:116-124; src/store/process.rs:114-125. Action errors are printed before shutdown, but a held process owner or shutdown error exits 1 silently even after successful action output. Not higher: durable recovery state is not rolled back and the process still exits as required. Smallest fix: print a plain shutdown or retained-owner diagnostic before exit without changing ownership bounds. Verify: exercise each failure after a successful action and inspect stderr and retained state.

title: Cover runbook refusal for missing inventory and snapshot reassignment
description: PR11 follow-up F35. Source in the inventory repair based on e0ec53f: tests/postgres/test_release_runbook.py:28-31. Its fifteen subcases catch the original complete-inventory narrowing, but do not exercise direct step5 with unset or empty inventory, or a sourced config assigning the readonly snapshot variable. Current code refuses these by inspection; no current false pass of the selected forwarding cases was demonstrated. P2 negative-coverage gap. Add actual-document-shell negative cases proving no migrate invocation and controlled failure for these inputs, while keeping the original old-document RED and fixed complete-inventory GREEN.

title: Saturation coverage does not isolate the engine observer refusal cause
description:
W8 test follow-up F19. Source: tests/postgres/w5_accounting.py:202-209,236-237; tests/postgres/w8.py:36-39.

The fixture proves a fresh ordinary observer is refused when capacity is full, but its engine alarm assertion only checks observer reconnect failed. Designated-standby admission can independently prevent reconnection. Attribute the engine refusal with its observed database reason before claiming capacity caused that particular failure; retain the independent fresh-observer refusal and out-of-band recovery proof.
notes: PR11 follow-up F34, deduplicated here. PR11 follow-up F34. Source at e0ec53f: tests/postgres/w5_accounting.py:201-279; tests/postgres/w8.py:saturate. Initial ordinary-capacity refusal is proved before the first out-of-band API stop. Stopping API backends and ending the original observer may free slots before standby resume; capacity at that later phase is not measured. The selected stop/pause/resume controls issue no fresh SQL, so the required initial outage and out-of-band path are demonstrated, but continuous exhaustion through every later step is not. P2 evidence-scope improvement, no demonstrated false pass of the stated initial-fault requirement. Measure/report each transition; if a future claim requires no ordinary slot at resume, add owned fixed clients and a fresh refusal check then. Keep reserved administrator assertions separate from recovery controls and verify all added clients are cleaned up. Rating P2 for the additional unmeasured capacity transitions; existing observer-cause attribution remains within this item.

title: Recovery documentation overstates the parent command result
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: docs/recovery.md:111-112 promises a row showing each action result, but src/bin/recovery.rs:77-79 prints only the incident; src/recovery.rs:268-280 stores parent disposition separately. The row cannot show which parent was confirmed or cancelled. Not higher: the acknowledged disposition remains durable. Smallest fix: describe the actual incident-only output and how to inspect the disposition, or return that result explicitly. Verify: compare both parent dispositions with stdout and retained rows.

title: rate_allowance's consume flag is always true
description:
Severity P3. Source: W5 audit item 10; carried as W6 Run item 11. Evidence at b037383: the only caller passes `true` (`src/api/mod.rs:199`), so the `consume` parameter (`:201`) and its branch (`:220`) are dead.

Fix: remove the parameter.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A fatal engine error emits duplicate operator alarms
description:
W8 follow-up F14. Source at aa1ad12: src/engine.rs:203-212; src/store/component.rs:387.

fatal_with_error emits the same alarm twice with different threshold_ms values. Keep one consistent fatal diagnostic while retaining the operator-action requirement.

title: Completion-only observer exhaustion lacks a direct transition trace
description:
W8 follow-up F18. Source at aa1ad12: src/store/commit.rs:184; src/store/accounting.rs:254.

The alarm exists, but there is no explicit trace distinguishing a COMMIT refused before dispatch by observer exhaustion from a deferred fatal exit with outstanding receipts. Add bounded transition evidence without changing COMMIT ownership or permitting an early checkout release.

title: An absent registered backend evicts a healthy commit observer
description:
Severity P2. Source: W5 Run (round 1); PR #6 review-bot thread on `accounting.rs:148`; carried as W6 Run item 1. Evidence at b037383: in `src/store/accounting.rs:127-155`, a missing activity row for one attempt's backend counts as lost observer visibility, closes a healthy observer and ends every other attempt's sample run.

Why not higher: accounting stays conservative (charges more, never less); no money effect.

Smallest fix: tell an absent attempt backend apart from hidden or failed observer evidence. Verify with two registered attempts where one backend exits, asserting the other keeps its exemption.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: W7 manifests claim no external effects and no recovery incidents
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: tests/postgres/harness.py:512-515; tests/postgres/w7.py:142-163. The W7 phase falls through to no external effects and always inherits the no-product-incidents limitation despite exercising recovery. Not higher: scenario assertions and child events remain available. Smallest fix: make coverage and limitation fields phase-accurate without rewriting historical raw evidence. Verify: compare a W7 manifest with its activated child events. Related pvr-q09 covers the W5 external-effects label; this finding also covers the W7 recovery-incidents claim.

title: Identity-mismatch case is not isolated from state rejection
description:
Severity P3. Source: PR #6 review-bot nitpick (Trivial). Evidence at b037383: `tests/postgres/w5_accounting.py:94-99` injects the identity mismatch while the backend is `idle:ClientRead`, so those samples would be rejected on state even if the matcher ignored `backend_start`. Lines 113-116 still catch an identity-reporting or missing-flag regression.

Fix: inject the mismatch during SyncRep and assert no extra exemption.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Older PRV-41 conformance anchor points one line early
description:
Severity P3. Source: W6 Run item 21 (round 3). Evidence at b037383: the older PRV-41 row in `docs/conformance-map.md` links `02-provider-contract.md:1267` (a blank line) instead of 1268. Navigation only.

Fix: point the anchor at 1268.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Fresh-install instructions omit the offline migration prerequisites
description:
W8 follow-up F3. Source at aa1ad12: README.md:154-163; docs/release.md.

The fresh-install example runs migrate while bootstrap leaves the application role LOGIN, and omits the mandatory PROVISIOND_APPLICATION_ROLES setting. Following that example now fails before migration. Align fresh-install instructions with the accepted offline gate and verify the documented clean-install sequence.

title: Retired-history reads scan the permanent retired table
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 20 (round 3). Evidence at b037383: `retired_operations` has only its id key (`migrations/0003-reconciliation.sql:175-180`), while `operation_history` (`src/api/mod.rs:31-35`) filters it by `id::text` equality and tenant and unions it into detail and list reads. The table is permanent and grows.

Why not higher: cost at large retired volumes was not measured and is beyond the represented scale.

Smallest fix: measure representative aged histories, then add matching access paths or index-usable predicates. Verify detail and list bounds and privacy. Related: the retained-history capacity item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Periodic pacing ignores provider throttle hints across remaining account calls
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 17 (a reader suggestion rated as a defect; round 1); widened by the W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: a throttled channel ends its page walk, but other account calls and the next one-second pass do not honour a longer retry hint (`src/engine/reconciliation.rs:321-356`, `src/bin/engine.rs:64-75`). The audit adds that the pass re-reads credential health in a transaction before every provider call.

Why not higher: absence handling fails closed; production pacing policy belongs to W8.

Smallest fix: in the pacing work, yield and coalesce account work using provider hints. Verify with an attributed throttle and the resulting call history.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Stale precommit accounting comment
description:
Severity P3. Source: W5 Run item 3 (round 1); carried as W6 Run item 3. Evidence at b037383: the comment at `src/engine.rs:199` says elapsed precommit work is charged separately; the code charges the whole attempt minus the attributed standby wait. Comment accuracy only.

Fix: align the comment with the arithmetic.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Remove redundant DDL transport event assertion
description: Severity P3. At bc435f3 tests/postgres/w8.py:116 the transport_closed event assertion repeats the proxy close_connection contract. Independent closed/close_source checks, exact connection-failure diagnostic, no lock timeout/retry, and the no-close negative demonstration already establish the planned interruption. No behavior or requirement changes. Consider reducing duplicate checks without weakening those independent guards.

title: Deferred observer exhaustion can be labelled ordinary retry exhaustion
description:
W8 follow-up F17. Source at aa1ad12: src/engine.rs:337,372.

A registration waiting for the completion-only observer-exhaustion drain can ultimately label its alarm ordinary Store retry exhaustion. Preserve the originating reason in the final diagnostic; owned sent COMMIT retention must remain unchanged.

title: The recovery decision links ordinary restart as standby rebuild evidence
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: docs/decisions.md:1748-1751 links scenario-w7_ordinary.json as ordinary restart/standby evidence. That file records w7_ordinary, while scenario-w7_rebuild.json records the separate standby rebuild. Not higher: the rebuild evidence exists and the canonical phase includes it; the documentation points at the wrong trace. Smallest fix: link the rebuild file separately and label the ordinary-restart scope accurately. Verify: follow both links and compare their recorded selector, scenario and bootstrap observations.

title: Concurrent harness invocations can lease each other's port blocks
description:
Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (the pull request's review bot). Evidence at 0185374: `tests/postgres/runner.py:26-38` gives each invocation a pool of every remaining ten-port block below 26000, and its reservation sockets bind with `SO_REUSEADDR`, so two invocations started with different `PROVISIOND_HARNESS_PORT_BASE` values can rotate into each other's live blocks and collide when their servers start.

Why not higher: the documented and gated use runs one canonical or iteration invocation per capped unit at a time, and a collision surfaces as a failed bind, never as a passing check.

Smallest fix: coordinate block ownership across invocations (for example a lock file per block under a shared directory) or confine each pool to an explicitly exclusive range. Verify with two concurrent invocations on adjacent bases that never share a block.

title: Account-pass observations get the pass-end instant
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/engine/reconciliation.rs:358,375-376` stamps every enumerated resource with one instant taken after all pages, so an older present state can overwrite a newer state observation. Gone writes use their own read's instant.

Why not higher: not shown to change a money decision; later observations correct the state.

Smallest fix: stamp each page with the instant of its own read. Verify with a state change between pages.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Operator profile documentation omits fixture rate expiry and refresh requirements
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (two readers). Evidence at eb75a02: migrations/0004-recovery.sql:102,144-161; src/api/mod.rs:1032-1034; README.md:121-172; docs/scope.md:277-285. Controlled rates expire 3600 seconds after their observation stamp, but profile documentation omits refresh and migration-age limits and consequent rate-unavailable refusals. Not higher: stale rates fail closed and production rate construction remains deferred. Smallest fix: document the actual fixture expiry and refresh procedure without changing bounds. Verify: age a fixture rate, observe refused rate-dependent work, then refresh and observe recovery.

title: An operator observed resolution can bind an already attached machine
description:
Severity P1 (re-rated from P2 on 2026-11-13; older than W7, review-preexisting): a money defect on a reachable path and a requirement made false (LDG-32): binding an already attached machine posts this operation's fee and unit debits again. The original "why not higher" below is superseded by this re-rate. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/api/operator.rs:422` and `src/store/business.rs:480` merge into the existing machine on `(provider_account, external_id)` for the same tenant and post this operation's fee and unit debits.

Why not higher: the open-commitment unique index refuses it while that machine has an open commitment, and it needs an authenticated operator decision.

Smallest fix: refuse an external id already attached to another operation. Verify with an operator resolution naming an attached machine.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).
close_reason: Observed resolution refuses another operation external identity before fee/unit debit, including same-tenant conflicts after original deletion. Historical runtime reproduces the extra simulated debit; final W6 case checks four 409 refusals without new debits or receipts. See evidence/w8/report.md and regressions.json. Live operator arm was not reachable.

title: F3: rail history beyond the 2 MiB response cap stops funding ingestion
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #5 known limits (F3); W5 Run deferred work; carried in PR #6 and #7. Evidence at b037383: the rail simulator returns its whole retained history on `GET /settlements` (`src/api/funding.rs:120-131`), and the client refuses any reply over 2 MiB (`src/http.rs:106`), about 8,000 observations. Past that, every poll fails as `rail_observation_unavailable` (`src/api/funding.rs:140`), so new payments are never credited, also after a restart. `docs/scope.md` records the limit.

Why not higher: no false credit or money loss; replies fail closed and the cap is far beyond the local profile's volumes.

Smallest fix: bounded delivery (a cursor or pages) that keeps replay, idempotency and restart behaviour. Verify with a history over the cap that still credits a new observation. Related: the funding watcher reprocessing item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Recovery reports omit the details needed to explain close refusal
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/bin/recovery.rs:66; src/recovery.rs:61-63,224-236; migrations/0004-recovery.sql:66-79. Report returns only the incident row, omitting held parent IDs and account/rate close obligations; close combines those three causes into one refusal. Not higher: close remains conservative and enforces its prerequisites. Smallest fix: include actionable parent identities and unmet close prerequisites in the report and refusal. Verify: exercise each prerequisite independently and identify the specific outstanding work from command output.

title: Legacy unresolved fixture's error text differs from the base literal
description:
Severity P3. Source: W6 Run item 23 (round 3). Evidence at b037383: `tests/postgres/w6_continuation.py:81` uses `engine restarted while operation was running`, while the base runtime used `interrupted by ordinary restart`. The migration never reads that text.

Fix: use the original literal, or say the text is not exact.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Backoff-budget probe has a 7 ms scheduling window
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #6 review-bot thread (Major); carried as W6 Run item 14. Evidence at b037383: the probe sleeps 1.993 s (`tests/postgres/w5.py:924`) and requires `1990 <= spent_ms < 2000` (`:932`); a scheduling delay over about 7 ms takes the fatal path before any retry, and the required selector fails.

Why not higher: false reds only; no broken run passes.

Smallest fix: a controlled retry clock or a test hook at the budget boundary, without changing the runtime budget. Verify by injecting scheduling delay.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Activation without a healthy provider account is never assigned later
description:
Severity P2. Source: W5 audit item 5; carried as W6 Run item 9. Evidence at b037383: activation inserts the only tenant-to-account assignment and just traces `activation_without_healthy_assignment` when no healthy account can be assigned (`src/api/funding.rs:81-88`), so the tenant keeps no provider account after accounts recover.

Why not higher: only fixtures change account status; whether the specification requires a later assignment is not yet assessed.

Smallest fix: assess the pinned specification first; then add the later assignment or document the limit with an account-recovery scenario.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A fence held by another episode closes the current one as funded
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/store/deletion.rs:82-94` closes the current cleanup episode as funded when the machine's fence belongs to another episode.

Why not higher: not shown reachable: each machine has at most one open delete episode and every close clears its fence.

Smallest fix: refuse or stall when the fence names another episode. Verify with a fixture holding a foreign fence.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Exclusive histories have no bounded admission order
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/runner.py:161-172 requires an exclusive worker to acquire every token at once, releasing partial acquisitions and polling; :185-204 upgrades W6 similarly while other workers compete. Exclusive histories serialize only after competing work drains, making elapsed time depend on scheduling. Not higher: isolation is preserved and no wrong verdict is shown. Smallest fix: document the scheduling limitation or give waiting exclusive work an explicit admission order without changing scenario timing bounds. Verify: schedule mixed ordinary and exclusive jobs and observe eventual admission and the same inventory.

title: The admission retry test name describes a different assertion
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/test_startup_retry.py:206-214 names its method test_engine_only_admission_check_events_can_repeat, but supplies only missing, post_read, test and unknown kinds and asserts an error with exactly one start. It checks rejection of non-admission kinds rather than the positive repeat path named. Not higher: naming only; those rejection assertions remain useful. Smallest fix: name the method for rejecting non-admission check kinds or separate the positive and negative examples clearly. Verify: compare each method name with its supplied kinds and asserted start count.

title: Commit observer reconnect and error churn without backoff
description:
Severity P2. Source: W5 Run (rated P2 by one reader, P3 by another); PR #6 review-bot thread on `accounting.rs:182`; carried as W6 Run item 2. Evidence at b037383: a failed checked reconnect retries on every 20 ms tick, even with nothing registered (`src/store/accounting.rs:159-197`), producing dozens of connect and log cycles in about 2.2 s in the mismatch runs.

Why not higher: availability and log noise; no wrong charge shown.

Smallest fix: pace reconnect failures and coalesce diagnostics within the existing bounds. Verify a bounded attempt and log count during a persistent failure, and recovery afterwards.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Recovery CLI usage errors are reported as operational alarms
description:
W8 follow-up F16. Source at aa1ad12: src/bin/recovery.rs:117.

Ordinary command-line usage mistakes emit operator_action_required. Separate usage diagnostics from an operational recovery failure while preserving nonzero exit status.

title: Service event files have no documented retention or space policy
description:
W8 follow-up F12. Source at aa1ad12: deploy/systemd/provisiond-engine@.service:41; deploy/systemd/provisiond-api@.service:41; docs/decisions.md D-70.

Append event files can grow at hundreds of records per second. A full filesystem can make output fail and spend supervisor starts, and rename-based rotation leaves the running process on the old file. Document measured retention, space monitoring and a supported rotation procedure for the accepted profile.

title: A failed port allocator thread can hang the canonical run
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/runner.py:47-73 lets request decoding, reservation bookkeeping, logging or reply errors end the allocator thread. Its listening socket remains open until context cleanup (:74-76); later port_request calls wait on an unbounded readline (:81-85). Not higher: fixture liveness only, with no incorrect product result. Smallest fix: propagate allocator failure to its owner and bound or interrupt pending requests. Verify: inject an allocator request/log failure and observe a nonzero run with owned cleanup instead of a stalled client.

title: Operators have no supported path to configure accounts, listings or rates
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: migrations/0002-local-service.sql:5-19; src/api/operator.rs:201-251; tests/postgres/workflow.py:70-74. This predates W7: fixtures populate accounts, listings and rates with SQL, and the operator listener has no configuration routes. Not higher: the supported prototype fails closed and no unauthorized financial effect is demonstrated. Smallest fix: define and document a supported operator configuration path consistent with the accepted profile. Verify: configure all three inputs through that path and use them in the customer workflow.

title: A tied or backward clock can reject an ordinary fixture rate input
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: migrations/0004-recovery.sql:116,123-128. The trigger clamps accepted_at to the previous time and defaults observed_at to it; a tied or backward clock can violate the per-currency observed_at uniqueness constraint. Not higher: this rejects a controlled input without demonstrated money or data corruption. Smallest fix: keep source observation and acceptance clocks distinct under STO-49 ordering and uniqueness. Verify: exercise ordinary rate writes across a tied and backward clock and check the exact expected outcome.

title: Bootstrap coverage omits simultaneous backup sender exclusion and migration checks
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (two readers). Evidence at eb75a02: tests/postgres/w7.py:186-197; tests/postgres/harness.py:301-341. The rebuild checks backup provenance, catch-up and no incident, but never observes simultaneous backup-sender exclusion or absence of migration during bootstrap. Not higher: this is missing evidence, with no demonstrated runtime guard violation. Smallest fix: add a focused owned bootstrap observation using existing machinery. Verify: activate the trace and observe sender exclusion and no migration during the actual backup.

title: Published W7 phase metadata omits the generated command prefix
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: evidence/w7/canonical-w7.json:311-320 starts its command with python3, while tests/postgres/harness.py:523 prepends nix develop --command and embedded children retain it (canonical-w7.json:1071-1077). publication-transform.json:8 claims full manifests changed only in paths/raw streams; a launcher-prefix removal is neither. Not higher: command provenance inconsistency, with exits and source hashes retained. Smallest fix: preserve the recorded command or explicitly document the metadata normalization without inventing a run. Verify: compare the published command with the retained original and declared transformation.

title: Assess service survival after brief connection check timeouts
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: docs/decisions.md:1889-1900 and evidence/w7/report.md:106-115 retain pre-publication failures: an admitted engine exited on a checkout deadline after its startup lock/generation advance; POST /v1/enrol returned retryable 503 "store checkout unavailable". src/entry.rs:46 sets 250 ms; src/api/mod.rs:86-91 supplies retry_after_ms=250. tests/postgres/workflow.py:247-259 excludes enrolment from retries. D-6 remains open for W8 (:1991-2007). Not higher: availability failures, no demonstrated wrong money/state; timing cause is inconclusive. Smallest fix: decide supported engine/API resilience and client retry behavior within existing ownership/fencing rules. Verify: controlled post-admission timeouts, recovery and paced enrolment retry. Related pvr-78v covers the separate retained-history load defect.
notes:
W8 partial completion: D-70 selects bounded post-admission engine startup/configuration retry, retryable API checkout refusal and a paced local customer policy. The recorded live journey proves bounded restarts and pretransaction overload behavior, but does not establish the issue requested controlled post-admission failure/recovery and paced enrolment retry. Keep this issue open pending that targeted verification. See evidence/w8/report.md and validation.json; implemented behavior is distinct from a demonstrated arm.
Source reading at 04b95a8: src/api/mod.rs:433-434 consumes the enrolment token before component.begin() at src/api/mod.rs:442 reaches connection checkout (src/store/component.rs:87-102; src/store/mod.rs:569-570,210-211). src/auth.rs:89-95 retains the consumed nonce and rejects reuse. After a checkout failure on this path, a retry with the identical body in the same process would therefore present an already consumed token. This is a reading of the source; no reproducer was run. The targeted post-admission recovery and paced enrolment verification requested by this bead should confirm or refute this reading first.
2026-11-24 targeted R1 at c5045df: source reading confirmed live. Customer received retryable 503 overloaded, waited 1.081186978 seconds (Retry-After 1 s exceeds body hint 250 ms), then identical bytes in the same API process received 400 invalid_request / invalid admission token; a fresh code succeeded. Diagnostic command exit 0 in 10.105560480 seconds, cleanup errors none. Sanitized record: evidence/kin/r1.json. Rated P1 under supported wrong behaviour / unmet acceptance: STO-55 requires retryable overloaded and DOM-17 makes same-request retry normative; D-70 promises enrolment retry, W8 scope and D-6 measured retry remain unmet. Smallest correction preserves code availability only after checkout refusal before a request transaction, retaining API-33 single use, API-40/WIR-12 validation precedence and no enrolment replay. No specification or owner policy change is selected. Full acceptance and engine recovery remain not run.

title: Two recovery decisions point to a stale candidate regression count
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (two readers). Evidence at 0185374: docs/decisions.md:1787-1788 (D-59) and :1831-1832 (D-63) link the current report while saying four candidate regressions. evidence/w7/regressions.json:3-4 records five; report.md:280-282 agrees. D-65 already supplies the final five-count at decisions.md:1896-1897, but the older links still lack precise historical scope. Not higher: historical wording, with the actual inventory intact. Smallest fix: identify the original four-case scope or link the final five-case addendum explicitly at both sentences. Verify: compare both references with the linked inventory.

title: A recovery log write failure omits guidance about the action outcome
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/bin/recovery.rs:48-50; src/recovery.rs:209-212. A diagnostic write can fail after the phase commit, yet stderr only says cannot write and exits 1 without explaining possible completion or how to inspect it. Not higher: the acknowledged phase remains retained and no false financial result is shown. Smallest fix: state that exit failure does not establish action failure and direct the operator to recovery report. Verify: fail logging after acknowledgment and compare the message with the retained phase.

title: Engine deployment retry eligibility ignores a paused standby
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/workflow.py:209-214 tests only unreleased proxy gates when computing armed; tests/postgres/scenarios.py:93-116 tracks a paused standby separately in h.paused. A future cold engine start with that fault could be misclassified as eligible for fixture repetition. Not higher: no current caller reaches this combination, and a paused standby still refuses the bounded attempts. Smallest fix: include the owned paused-standby fault in retry exclusion. Verify: a paused-standby cold start is recorded once and refused without repetition.

title: The full suite phase count guard compares a derived count with itself
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/harness.py:602-617 constructs records by iterating phases, then checks len(records)==len(phases). Removing a required phase also changes that expected count, so the runtime guard cannot detect an incomplete declared inventory. Only tests/postgres/test_iteration.py:74-76 independently pins twelve. Not higher: the current twelve-phase inventory is intact and the unit pin catches edits when run. Smallest fix: validate the full selector against an independently maintained required phase set/count. Verify: omit one required phase and require the full invocation to refuse it.

title: Recovery usage omits prepare, parent and close
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/bin/recovery.rs:67-80,112. The command supports prepare, close and parent but its usage error advertises none of them. Not higher: this affects discovery rather than command execution. Smallest fix: list the supported actions and arguments in usage. Verify: compare usage output with each accepted command form.

title: Prepare can print a successor incident instead of the incident it prepared
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/recovery.rs:157-168,196-213; src/bin/recovery.rs:70-71. Prepare captures and acknowledges one incident, then the command separately reads whichever incident is currently open; supersession between those operations can change the printed identity. Not higher: the prepared transaction checks incident identity and no incorrect write is demonstrated. Smallest fix: return the prepared identity and read its retained row. Verify: supersede between preparation and output and verify the printed identity matches the prepared incident.

title: The release runbook omits installation of its service templates
description:
W8 follow-up F6. Source at aa1ad12: docs/release.md:4; deploy/systemd/provisiond-engine@.service; deploy/systemd/provisiond-api@.service.

Later runbook steps operate on instance services but the preparation never copies the templates into the user unit directory or reloads the supervisor. Document and verify the complete installation prerequisite for a fresh operator environment.

title: Upgraded machines' pre-upgrade time is absorbed as a rate outage
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `migrations/0003-reconciliation.sql:116-121` seeds the rate history at migration time, so exit accounting finds no rate in force before the upgrade and records that span as an operator `rate_outage` deficiency instead of a customer debit.

Why not higher: only a schema-2 database with billable machines reaches it, and none is deployed.

Smallest fix: seed the rate history from each machine's frozen terms at its meter seed. Verify by upgrading a schema-2 fixture with a billable machine and checking its exit accounting.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: The sustained and fatal observer alarms fire at the same bound
description:
W8 follow-up F10. Source at aa1ad12: src/store/accounting.rs:222-228.

At the 2000 ms observer reconnect bound the sustained warning and fatal alarm fire together. Clarify their relationship and avoid presenting them as separately measured warning periods.

title: Balance totals and commitments are read in two snapshots
description:
Severity P1 (older than this change; re-rated from a deferred known limit). Source: PR #5 known limits (WIR-16); carried in PR #6 and PR #7. Evidence at master b037383: `GET /v1/balance?commitments=true` reads its totals in one statement (`src/api/mod.rs:944`) and its commitments page in another (`src/api/mod.rs:949-951`, `page` at :971). A create or settlement committing between the two breaks WIR-16's `committed_sats == sum(reserved_sats)` (spec 13-wire-contract.md:652-655): a caller sees a body whose totals contradict its own commitments.

Why P1: wrong behaviour in a supported read (a wire invariant made false). Not P0: no money moves, the read is advisory.

Smallest fix: read totals and the page in one snapshot (one REPEATABLE READ transaction, or one statement). Verify with a test that commits a create between the two reads and asserts the equality.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Funding watcher reprocesses the whole rail history every 100 ms
description:
Severity P2 (re-rated from P3 by the follow-up ledger review for linear database and log load; the W6 Run report still lists it as P3). Source: W5 audit item 8; carried as W6 Run item 10. Evidence at b037383: every 100 ms tick (`src/api/funding.rs:142`) re-runs each retained final observation, credited or not: a binding read, a write transaction with the tenant serialization lock and COMMIT, and a trace line (`src/api/funding.rs:133-135`), on the API's single read and write sessions. 1,000 retained observations give about 10,000 transactions and trace lines a second.

Why not higher: no customer refusal was measured; the watcher releases its session between observations.

Smallest fix: skip observations already credited, or use a delivery cursor, preserving replay semantics. Verify bounded transactions per tick with a large credited history. Related: the F3 rail-history item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: The LOGIN prerequisite negative shares its diagnostic with other refusals
description:
W8 test follow-up F20. Source: tests/postgres/w8.py:52-53.

The first offline-gate negative enables LOGIN but checks only the shared offline prerequisite refused prefix. A surviving-session refusal uses that same prefix. Assert the LOGIN-specific role state and zero surviving backends to distinguish this negative case; preserve unchanged migration history and the separate surviving-session case.

title: A permanently invalid retained payment record blocks recovery replay
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (two readers). Evidence at eb75a02: src/api/funding.rs:50-54,139-143,182-217; src/api/mod.rs:1326-1328. A wrong-hash settlement for a retained deposit propagates its per-record error before later valid observations or step 3; startup cannot open its listener. Not higher: trusted-adapter invalid evidence fails closed without false credit. Smallest fix: define source-consistent handling of permanent record invalidity separately from transient store or commit uncertainty. Verify: replay a bad bound record before valid history without losing valid acknowledged credit. Only the per-record defect is drafted; pvr-9rn already covers non-array replies.

title: Raw W5 external-effects label omits w5
description:
Severity P2. Source: W5 Run item 4 (Implementer); PR #6 review-bot outside-diff comment; carried as W6 Run item 4. Evidence at b037383: the manifest predicate at `tests/postgres/harness.py:451` labels phase `w5` "not applicable: no external effects" although W5 records nested simulator effects. The evidence manifest therefore states something false about W5.

Why not higher: nested effects stay recorded and the sanitized summaries are correct.

Smallest fix: add `w5` to the simulator-evidence branch of the label. Verify by asserting the W5 manifest's classification.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: The ephemeral overlap unit assumes the lowest valid port base
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/test_ports.py:30-38 mocks the ephemeral range as base+499..base+600, but harness.py:39-43 checks the fixed 25500..25999 range. With valid base 25510 the mock becomes 26009..26110, so no overlap is detected and the later directory mock raises the wrong error. Not higher: a false unit failure for a supported fixture configuration; product isolation still holds. Smallest fix: use the actual reserved-range boundary or explicitly scope the test base. Verify: run the unit with lowest and nonlowest valid bases and require the intended overlap refusal before side effects.

title: The incident startup example starts the API before its prerequisite acknowledgement
description:
W8 follow-up F13. Source at aa1ad12: docs/release.md:185-188; docs/recovery.md:331-334.

With an open incident the example starts the API without waiting for recovery_step_acknowledged step 2; the acknowledgement is only a comment. Refused API starts consume the bounded start budget. Make the prerequisite an executed, checked step and verify the incident-start sequence.

title: Stale publication sentence in the W5 report
description:
Severity P3. Source: W5 publication audit; carried as W6 Run item 6. Evidence at b037383: `evidence/w5/report.md:20` says "Nothing was pushed, merged or published.", true when recorded and false since PR #6 merged. Wording only.

Fix: date the sentence or add a publication note, without changing the recorded evidence.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A legacy machine without native terms stops the engine at its cleanup
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/store/deletion.rs:91` treats missing native terms as no rate, so the cleanup reaches the stopped no-rate path and exits the engine.

Why not higher: same no-fence, no-call stop as the no-rate item; only legacy rows lack terms and none is deployed.

Smallest fix: give legacy machines their terms at migration or classify them separately. Verify with a legacy machine queued for cleanup. Related: the no-rate engine-exit item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Provider evidence can be frozen before the simulator's last record
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #6 review-bot thread (Minor); carried as W6 Run item 13. Evidence at b037383: the simulator records `read_response_returned` after the reply is delivered (`tests/postgres/simulator.py:281`), so the snapshot in `tests/postgres/w5.py:354-365` can miss it and the later exact equality fails.

Why not higher: fails closed on a missing final event.

Smallest fix: wait for the attributed completion record before freezing evidence, here and in the other full-trace comparisons. Verify by delaying the record in the simulator.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Restore application login before saturation recovery application checks
description: PR11 follow-up F32. Source at e0ec53f: docs/recovery.md:306-318. When earlier offline-release work left the application role NOLOGIN, application --check-schema calls precede login restoration and fail. The documented stop-on-error keeps components masked, so this is a fail-closed availability limit, P2 rather than an unsafe release. Move the acknowledged-migration-dependent login restoration ahead of application checks while retaining masks and administrative checks. Verify the prior-NOLOGIN recovery path succeeds only after required migration acknowledgement and failed checks never start components.

title: Meter quarantine does not stop the cleanup funding decision
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/store/deletion.rs:55-58` derives runway from the meter of a quarantined machine before fencing, while LDG-72 quarantines exhaustion decisions for that subject.

Why not higher: quarantine is set only by the migration audit.

Smallest fix: check quarantine before the funding decision and hold the cleanup. Verify with a quarantined machine queued for cleanup.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Supervised recovery opens its log before watching the parent pipe
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/bin/recovery.rs:16-40. The synchronous diagnostic open precedes watcher creation; opening a FIFO without a reader can block before parent death is observed. Not higher: this requires a blocking diagnostic target before recovery work and no unsafe write is demonstrated. Smallest fix: start parent-pipe supervision before opening diagnostics. Verify: block the log open, close the parent pipe and observe child termination without recovery writes.

title: Housekeeping skip handling catches more than checkout failures
description:
W8 follow-up F9. Source at aa1ad12: src/api/mod.rs:1539; docs/decisions.md D-70.

The freeze, probe and begin error branches skip every error, while the recorded policy describes handling transient checkout and connection-check refusal. Classify supported retryable errors explicitly and ensure unrelated permanent or invariant errors remain actionable.

title: Historical W6 baseline commands require unpublished commits
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/w6_blocking_baseline.py:18,36,43-48 archives/fetches ac83e17, 96c6001 or ab01486, none ancestral to master or this tip. A fresh published-history clone lacks these inputs. This predates W7. README.md:30-31,66-91 requires check.sh and the canonical suite; tools/check.sh:6-15 and tools/postgres.sh:5 do not call this standalone script. docs/decisions.md:1722-1731 records its historical proof, not a recurring gate. Thus P2, not older P1: reproducibility loss without a blocked required gate. Smallest fix: retain accessible protected baseline sources or map proven identical published commits. Verify: reproduce each exact red from a fresh clone.

title: Migration lock and role-gate errors use an acquisition-stage label
description:
W8 follow-up F4. Source at aa1ad12: src/store/migration.rs:123.

Lock-timeout and application-role-gate errors retain the connection-stage labels initial acquisition or reconnect, even after connection establishment. Clarify stage wording while keeping the required initial-acquisition diagnostic and bounded retry behavior.

title: Terminating the iteration script alone leaves its children running
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (two readers). Evidence at 0185374: tools/iteration.sh:7-25 runs foreground commands without signal forwarding or child supervision. TERM addressed only to the script can leave the harness and its PostgreSQL descendants running; tools/postgres.sh:5 instead replaces its shell with the harness. Not higher: invocation-wide cgroup termination remains available; no cross-run product corruption is shown. Smallest fix: forward termination to the owned child and await its cleanup while preserving command exits. Verify: signal only the iteration script PID during a live phase and observe all owned descendants exit and cleanup evidence survive.

title: Retirement table header comment omits the new kind and machine metadata
description:
Severity P3. Source: W6 Run item 25 (round 6). Evidence at b037383: the header comment in `migrations/0003-reconciliation.sql:173-180` describes only identity, ownership and horizon, while `kind` and `machine_id` now support retained validation; the inline comment explains them.

Fix: make the header and inline comment agree.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Concurrent recovery commands can interleave records in a shared log
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (two readers). Evidence at eb75a02: src/bin/recovery.rs:18-23,43-50. Each process has its own mutex around formatted writes to an append file; formatting may issue multiple writes, so commands sharing a log lack whole-record serialization. Not higher: this affects diagnostic integrity without demonstrated corruption of durable recovery state. Smallest fix: encode each record before a write and ensure whole-record serialization across processes. Verify: run concurrent commands against one log and parse every complete JSON record.

title: Listener reservation errors can hide the scenario failure evidence
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/workflow.py:349-370 reaps children, then calls reserve_api_ports before recording application traces and simulator evidence. That reservation logs and rethrows OSError at :153-161. A busy listener port can therefore replace an existing scenario error and omit its principal evidence. Not higher: the run still fails; no broken product run passes. Smallest fix: retain the original failure and collect evidence before attempting reservation, preserving both errors. Verify: combine a scenario assertion failure with a reservation refusal and retain both causes, traces and cleanup.

title: Request headers are read one byte per syscall
description:
Severity P3. Source: W5 audit item 10; carried as W6 Run item 11. Evidence at b037383: `src/http.rs:25-28` reads headers one byte per `read` call, up to 16 KiB per request. No behaviour change required.

Fix: buffer the reads, preserving the header limits.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Expected negative API starts are recorded as failed fixture deployments
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: tests/postgres/w4_round2.py:133-136 and tests/postgres/w4_regressions.py:128-138 send intentional configuration/polling-budget refusals to deployment_exit. tests/postgres/workflow.py:39-41 labels every such event api_fixture_deployment_exit with result=fail, like a genuine deployment failure. Not higher: scenario assertions still distinguish expected refusal and preserve the real exit. Smallest fix: identify expected negative starts explicitly in the event classification while retaining exit evidence. Verify: compare an intended startup refusal with an unexpected ordinary deployment exit.

title: Commit failure can retain an earlier retry error as its diagnostic
description:
W8 follow-up F15. Source at aa1ad12: src/engine.rs:340-349.

A failed COMMIT does not refresh last_error, so later retry exhaustion can cite an earlier checkout or connection-check refusal. Preserve the relevant final error without changing uncertainty classification or retry policy.

title: Recovery documentation implies the log is needed to retain the loss report
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: docs/recovery.md:81-84 tells direct users to set the log variable to retain the report. The incident retains its reporting evidence and is returned by report/prepare (src/recovery.rs:45-52,61-67,158-164; src/bin/recovery.rs:66-71). Not higher: wording only; durable evidence is present. Smallest fix: distinguish retaining trace diagnostics from retaining and reading the incident report. Verify: run direct preparation without a log and compare stdout and a later report with the retained incident.

title: Reduce repeated W8 diagnostic construction
description: W8 final Standards follow-up F31. Source at 35ecf701: src/api/mod.rs:1540,1550,1560 and src/engine.rs:232-245. Three housekeeping stages repeat the skipped-tick trace/error-context construction, and startup retry repeats the same exhaustion diagnostic around the necessary before/after-backoff budget checks. P3 maintenance only, no policy or output mismatch observed. Factor construction locally where it improves clarity while retaining both budget checks and every stage. Related pvr-0ti owns the separate missing diagnostic-cause behavior; do not count this as fixing it. Verify stage names, error contexts, exhaustion reason and timing bounds stay unchanged.

title: Record separate test source identity for alarm regression red
description: Severity P3. The W8 alarm regression RED used an earlier draft of tests/postgres/test_w7_operator.py: its preserved traceback points to lines 33/37 while the final six-test file places the corresponding calls at 81/85. The actual RED is the intended old-helper assertion and the final GREEN exercises the same captured legitimate alarm and invalid-output alternatives. Preserve the test draft identity separately when documenting historical RED provenance; no behavioral effect.

title: A nonhealthy account can prevent recovery incident closure indefinitely
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/recovery.rs:233-236; src/engine/reconciliation.rs:295-302. Close requires a second completed pass for every configured account, while periodic passes run only for healthy accounts. Not higher: this conservatively blocks closure without a demonstrated destructive or financial outcome. Smallest fix: resolve account completion obligations against STO-54/56 and implement only a supported status transition. Verify: cover closure with a nonhealthy account while preserving authentication stops and avoiding invented absence.

title: Historical W7 references lack published commit mappings
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (one reader). Evidence at 0185374: .beads/issues.jsonl:4-61 retains eb75a02 citations in 22 W7 issues. evidence/w7/regressions.json:7, controls.json:360, canonical-controls.json:360, phase-metrics.json:135 and prior-failure.json:4 retain 20710b0 without a map to 8339aae, now pinned by tests/postgres/candidate_reds.py:9. prior-failure.json:20 retains cbc87dd. live-journey.json:4-39 partially maps eb75a02 to 06b7636 but leaves a moving HEAD comparison. Not higher: provenance/navigation gaps, with source hashes and results retained. Smallest fix: publish explicit old-to-new mappings and bind the journey comparison to f302686; preserve observed identities. Verify: resolve each rewritten target and compare its protected source map.

title: Published tracker entries expose the repository host path
description: Severity P2. Source: W7 recovery incidents test-suite review (three readers). Evidence at 0185374: .beads/issues.jsonl:1-63 contains absolute source_repo_path values in all 63 open entries, including the 41 older records and 22 W7 records. This predates W7 and publishes host-specific identifying metadata in the public tracker export. Not higher: a local path is exposed, not a demonstrated credential or runtime authority. Smallest fix: remove or normalize host-specific metadata from published exports while retaining local tracker operation and stable issue identities.
