Verify: scan the export for absolute host paths and confirm issue identities and import behavior remain intact.

title: Pass alarm classification independently of diagnostic wording
description: W8 final Standards follow-up F28. Source at 35ecf701: src/engine.rs:198-212. fatal_with_error selects the alarm threshold through reason.contains("retry exhausted"). Current callers use matching fixed strings and no wrong threshold was observed; this is a maintainability heuristic, P3. Pass a small alarm classification or explicit threshold independently of free-text diagnostics. Verify existing immediate and retry-exhaustion alarm values remain unchanged without making message edits control policy.

title: Schema-2 descriptor snapshots fail the new descriptor validation
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/pricing.rs:278` now requires `delete_shape`, `surviving_attachments` and `negative_seconds`; queued creates admitted under schema 2 fail at dispatch after the upgrade, and old provider descriptors refuse startup.

Why not higher: fails closed, and no schema-2 database is deployed.

Smallest fix: migrate stored snapshots and descriptors to the new fields, or default them on read. Verify a schema-2 queued create dispatches after the upgrade.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: An excluded no-rate cleanup decision exits the whole engine
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 15 (two readers; round 1). Evidence at b037383: when a cleanup reaches the no-rate decision (`src/engine/deletion.rs:63-66`), it traces `delete_no_rate_stopped` and returns `fatal`, so the error propagates out of the engine and stops all other work. Test: `tests/postgres/w6.py:370-375`.

Why not higher: the stopped path writes no fence and makes no provider call, so no money moves; only fixtures write rates, and OPS-41 steps 4-5 are left out by decision (D-46).

Smallest fix: when the no-rate lifecycle is in scope, isolate the stopped path so unrelated work continues. Verify unrelated work continues after a no-rate stop. Related: the legacy-machine-without-terms item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A missing named reporting file is reported as unsupplied input
description: Severity P3. Source: W7 fast-lane live test / review (one reader). Evidence at eb75a02: src/bin/recovery.rs:86-101. A configured nonexistent file takes the same branch as an unset path and prints no reporting input supplied without naming the missing path. Not higher: establishment intentionally continues with unknown endpoints. Smallest fix: distinguish unset input from a missing named file in the diagnostic. Verify: compare unset and nonexistent paths while checking both remain nonblocking.

title: Dispatch deadlines come from the startup descriptor, not the frozen terms
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #5 known limits; W5 Run deferred work. Evidence at b037383: `Dispatcher::load` reads every provider descriptor once at engine start (`src/engine/dispatch.rs:13-26`) and dispatch takes its deadlines from that catalog (`src/engine/dispatch.rs:218`), not from the terms frozen at admission. A descriptor change plus a restart between admission and dispatch can make a provider call wait longer than its reserve priced.

Why not higher: descriptors change only by operator configuration; no supported path changes them mid-flight.

Smallest fix: take dispatch deadlines from the admission's frozen terms. Verify by changing the descriptor between admission and dispatch and asserting the frozen deadline is used.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Add diagnostic identity guards to the default-resolution witness
description: Severity P3. In the W8 default-resolution fixture, opening and closing snapshots record the target id, provider account and wait end, but the witness helper does not explicitly compare identity fields with the target. The SQL WHERE operation id and immutable account assignment already bind the actual run, so this has no behavioral effect. At the final W8 fixture, tests/postgres/w6_edges.py:default_resolution_witness checks a stable window/cutoff and provider records are filtered by command id. Consider explicit diagnostic assertions when maintaining this helper; no policy or runtime change is needed.

title: Bind saturation attribution follow-up to an immutable source
description: Severity P3. The line anchors in pvr-alp refer to the pre-repair W5 fixture while bc435f3 moved the target block. The attribution question remains valid; the issue does not name an immutable baseline for its original line numbers. Record the relevant revision or symbol when revisiting it. No runtime or assertion effect.

title: DOM-21 conformance row still says the receiptless gap remains
description:
Severity P3. Source: W6 Run item 22 (round 3). Evidence at b037383: `docs/conformance-map.md:290` says "receiptless gap remains", which W6's receiptless retirement (retired identities that read as gone) has made stale. Status prose only.

Fix: update the row against the retained-identity evidence.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).
